dod_intent_evidence: Own SBIR abstract: $1.5M Air Force 2023 Phase II 'Spacehaven Synthetic Data Generation Software for Autonomous Space Domain Awareness and In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM)'; homepage explicitly lists 'Defense & ISR' as a configured domain with KLV/CoT/Firestorm integration and offline capability.
score_evidence: 'Runs where the mission is: Cloud, on-prem, or edge hardware when the network isn't an option — including Jetson-class devices. Plugs into the systems operators already run: Firestorm, CoT, GIS, BIM, CMMS' — MISB KLV/CoT/Firestorm and offline-capable framing shows deep TAK/DDIL fluency → deployment_awareness_absence (scored very low)

'Operators get a decision-ready answer in the form they can act on' and 'handing operators decision-ready intelligence' appear repeatedly in the core product pitch → operator_absence (scored very low)

Only open role: 'Full-Stack Product & Field Engineer – AI Systems' — explicitly tasked to 'deploy, configure, and troubleshoot AI systems in operational and field environments' and 'travel to customer locations, military installations, and test events' → hiring_profile_skew (scored very low, this IS a field-deployment hire)

'We're a small team solving hard problems at the intersection of AI, perception, and real-world deployment' — one hybrid field/product/AI hire covering two live product lines (Sentinel + Seahaven) and an active Air Force Phase II SBIR → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/STIG language anywhere despite explicitly targeting 'defense ISR' and integrating with Firestorm/CoT military systems, and despite claiming Sentinel is already 'fielded.'
blind_spots.operator_reality: A perception system ingesting ISR sensor feeds and drafting SALUTE reports needs an Authority to Operate before it touches a real government network; the deployment-architecture story here is unusually mature everywhere except this one gate, which is the gate that actually kills transitions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Public site voice is built around edge/offline engineering maturity (a genuinely rare strength), which may be masking that the compliance/paperwork side hasn't kept pace.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Configures per domain: defense ISR, infrastructure inspection, long-dwell monitoring.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Claims offline/edge operation 'when the network isn't an option, including Jetson-class devices,' but never states the SWaP-C budget for running the full agentic reasoning stack (working memory, tool use, multi-skill library) on that hardware.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An agent that reasons across frames, calls tools, and maintains working memory is compute- and power-hungry; without a stated thermal/power envelope, 'runs on Jetson-class devices' could mean a rack-mounted Jetson cluster or a single low-power module — the difference decides whether it fits the platform an operator actually carries.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Marketing emphasizes capability breadth (the reasoning pipeline) over the hardware constraints that would let a buyer size an actual deployment.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Edge · On‑prem · Cloud Runs where the mission runs

blind_spots.blind_spot: One open req (Full-Stack Product & Field Engineer) is asked to cover software development, AI engineering, customer engagement, and field deployment across military installations and test events simultaneously, for a 13-person team running two live products plus an active Phase II SBIR.
blind_spots.operator_reality: That single hybrid hire is the entire feedback loop between what breaks in the field and what gets fixed in the code — if that person is unavailable during a critical test event or installation, there's no visible backup, which is exactly the kind of single point of failure that turns a funded-months clock into a missed transition.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is intentionally lean and generalist by design ('we're a small team solving hard problems'), which is a strength for iteration speed but a risk for sustained field support at scale.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: One day you may be implementing a new product feature, the next analyzing model performance on a large dataset, debugging a deployment at a customer site, or supporting an operational exercise.

opener_hook: Sentinel already ingests MISB KLV, CoT, and Firestorm and runs offline on Jetson-class edge hardware — where's the ATO/RMF conversation for putting that on an actual ISR network?
what_they_do: Sentinel is an agentic computer-vision perception system that ingests ISR/drone/sensor feeds (KLV/CoT/Firestorm), geolocates detections, and drafts SALUTE reports for operators, edge-deployable and offline-capable; Seahaven is a companion synthetic 3D training-data engine. Used for defense ISR, space domain awareness (Air Force SBIR Phase II), infrastructure inspection, and industrial robotics.
